title: Inverse image preserves sheaf differentials
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common universe of sheaf values, and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits. Let $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ for the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, where ring differentials are those of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; this is a sheaf of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with the derivation induced by the sectionwise universal derivations. Equip inverse images of rings and modules with the operations induced by the finite-product comparisons of $f^{-1}$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaves $f^{-1}\Omega_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{f^{-1}\mathcal B/f^{-1}\mathcal A}$ which carries the inverse image of the universal derivation to the universal derivation. It is natural in commutative squares of sheaves of rings, and its comparisons for identity and composite geometric morphisms agree with the identity and composite inverse-image comparisons.

source.place: Tags 08TP (lemma-differentials-sheafify) and 08TQ (lemma-pullback-differentials); naturality and composition are the universal-derivation comparisons in these constructions.
